renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: read_distribution
  title: Reads per reference sequence
  description: |-
    Each dot is a reference sequence in a library: its size is the share of the library's reads on that sequence and its colour the log10 read count. It answers whether reads spread over the genome as expected.
    How to read: dots should grow with the length of the sequence, and the libraries should look alike. A sequence with a disproportionate share, such as the mitochondrial genome, or a library whose pattern differs from its peers points to a problem to fix before calling peaks.
    Source: https://github.com/ParkerLab/ataqv
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: chromosome
    mean_expression: log10_read_count
    frac_expressing: fraction_of_reads

- component: figure
  title: Share of reads per reference sequence
  description: |-
    Each bar is a reference sequence in a library: the fraction of its reads that fall on it. It answers which sequences take the largest part of each library.
    How to read: compare the bars between libraries. Large sequences should take larger shares, and any sequence standing out of that order deserves a look. ataqv reports no cut-off for this share, so none is drawn.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: chromosome
    y: fraction_of_reads
    color: sample
    labels:
      chromosome: Reference sequence
      fraction_of_reads: Share of reads
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Reads per reference sequence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of reads counted by ataqv, and the bars rank the sequences that hold most of them. It answers where the reads of the run go.
    How to read: the leaders should be the longest sequences. A short sequence among them is a sign of enrichment or contamination.
  column: read_count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: total reads, with the busiest sequences ranked

- component: card
  title: Largest share on one sequence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest share of a library's reads found on a single reference sequence, and the bars rank the libraries with the highest one. It answers whether a library is dominated by one sequence.
    How to read: a high value is expected for a long chromosome and is worrying for a short one. ataqv defines no cut-off for it, so no pass mark is drawn.
  column: fraction_of_reads
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: highest share of reads on a single sequence, with the libraries ranked

- component: card
  title: Spread of read shares
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads on a reference sequence, and the box shows how the shares spread. It answers how evenly the reads are shared out.
    How to read: a wide box with a long upper whisker means a few sequences take most of the reads. A tight box means an even spread over sequences of similar size.
  column: fraction_of_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share per sequence, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Read counts per sequence
  description: |-
    Each row is a reference sequence in a library with its read count, share of the reads and log10 read count. It answers the exact values behind the dot plot.
    How to read: sort by share to find the busiest sequences, or filter to one library to compare it with its peers.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fragment_ladder
  title: Fragment length ladder
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the share of reads at each fragment length. It answers whether the library shows the open-chromatin peak and the nucleosome ladder expected of ATAC-seq.
    How to read: a good library has a peak of short fragments followed by a decaying ladder with a bump near one nucleosome. A flat curve with no ladder points to over-tagmentation or damaged chromatin. Compare libraries and open the quality table for the ratio between the two windows.
    Lines and annotations: the shaded bands are the two windows ataqv counts, 50 to 100 bp for short fragments and 150 to 200 bp for mononucleosomal ones, taken from the ataqv source code. The ENCODE ATAC-seq standards also require a nucleosome-free region and a mononucleosome peak.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ParkerLab/ataqv/master/src/cpp/Metrics.cpp and https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Fragment length (bp)
    y_title: Share of all reads
    log_y: true
    shaded_bands:
    - - 50
      - 100
      - Short fragments (50-100 bp)
    - - 150
      - 200
      - Mononucleosomal (150-200 bp)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: fragment_length
    y: fraction_of_all_reads

- component: figure
  title: Fragment length distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the share of reads at each fragment length. It answers the same question as the ladder as a plain curve.
    How to read: look for a first peak below 100 bp and a second, lower one near 200 bp. A library without them lost the pattern of accessible chromatin.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_length
    y: fraction_of_all_reads
    color: sample
    labels:
      fragment_length: Fragment length (bp)
      fraction_of_all_reads: Share of all reads
      sample: Library

- component: figure
  title: Reads per fragment class
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library, split by the fragment class ataqv counts: short (50 to 100 bp), mononucleosomal (150 to 200 bp) or outside those windows. It answers how the reads of each library divide between open and nucleosomal fragments.
    How to read: a larger short class than mononucleosomal one is the signature of open chromatin. Libraries that differ in their split should not be compared directly.
    Lines and annotations: the class windows are ataqv's own, from its source code.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ParkerLab/ataqv/master/src/cpp/Metrics.cpp
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: read_count
    color: fragment_class
    labels:
      sample: Library
      read_count: Reads
      fragment_class: Fragment class

- component: card
  title: Reads per fragment class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads in the table, and the bars rank the fragment classes that hold most of them. It answers which kind of fragment dominates the run.
    How to read: the short and mononucleosomal classes should hold a large part of the reads. A large class outside the windows is a sign of fragments ataqv does not count in its ratio.
    Lines and annotations: the class windows are 50 to 100 bp and 150 to 200 bp, from the ataqv source code.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ParkerLab/ataqv/master/src/cpp/Metrics.cpp
  column: read_count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: fragment_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: total reads, with the classes ranked

- component: table
  title: Fragment length histogram
  description: |-
    Each row is a fragment length in a library with its read count, share of all reads and class. It answers the exact values behind the ladder.
    How to read: filter to one library and look at the lengths with the largest shares.

- component: advanced_viz
  title: TSS enrichment against reads in peaks
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its TSS enrichment on the horizontal axis and the percentage of its high-quality autosomal alignments that fall inside peaks on the vertical axis, with the marker sized by the number of peaks. It answers whether a library has both signal and specificity.
    How to read: good libraries sit to the right and above the line. A library high on one axis and low on the other has a good enrichment but poor specificity, or the reverse, and the two cards below give the cut-offs for each.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is 30 percent, the ENCODE ATAC-seq standard of 0.3 for the fraction of reads in peaks (0.2 is acceptable). ataqv computes the percentage on high-quality autosomal alignments, so the two are close but not identical.
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: TSS enrichment
    y_title: High-quality alignments in peaks (%)
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 30
    reference_label: ENCODE fraction of reads in peaks, 0.3
  roles:
    x: tss_enrichment
    y: hqaa_overlapping_peaks_percent
    color: sample
    size: total_peaks

- component: card
  title: TSS enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average TSS enrichment, the signal at transcription start sites over the flanks of the same window. It answers whether the libraries show the open chromatin expected of good ATAC-seq.
    How to read: higher is better. A library under the lower line has too little signal to trust its peaks, so check the fragment ladder and the TSS profile.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-offs are the ENCODE values for the GRCh38 RefSeq TSS annotation, 7 and above is ideal, 5 to 7 acceptable and under 5 concerning. The values depend on the annotation, so other references use other cut-offs (hg19 6 and 10, mm10 10 and 15).
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/
  column: tss_enrichment
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 7.0
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 5.0
  caption: average enrichment, with the lowest and highest library
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Peaks called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peaks ataqv saw in the peak files, and the bars rank the libraries with the most. It answers how much accessible chromatin each library resolves.
    How to read: a library with far fewer peaks than its peers has less usable signal. The count depends on depth and on the peak caller, so compare libraries of one run only.
  column: total_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: total peaks, with the libraries calling most ranked

- component: card
  title: Mitochondrial reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median fraction of reads that map to the mitochondrial genome, and the box shows the spread between libraries. It answers how much sequencing was wasted on mitochondrial DNA.
    How to read: lower is better, since mitochondrial reads carry no nuclear signal. A library far above the box is a candidate for a cleaner preparation. ataqv sets no cut-off for it, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://github.com/ParkerLab/ataqv
  column: mitochondrial_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median fraction of reads on the mitochondrial genome, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Reads in peaks
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percentage of high-quality autosomal alignments that overlap a peak. It answers how specific the signal is to accessible regions.
    How to read: higher is better. A low value means most reads lie in the background, so the library needs more depth or a cleaner preparation.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-offs are the ENCODE ATAC-seq standard for the fraction of reads in peaks, above 30 percent is good and above 20 percent acceptable. ataqv computes the percentage on high-quality autosomal alignments, a close but not identical quantity.
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/
  column: hqaa_overlapping_peaks_percent
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 30.0
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 20.0
  caption: average percent of alignments in peaks, with the lowest and highest library

- component: card
  title: Duplicate reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average fraction of reads that are duplicates, and the histogram shows how the libraries spread. It answers how much complexity was lost to PCR duplication.
    How to read: lower is better. A library at the right of the histogram has few distinct fragments and will add little at greater depth. ataqv defines no duplicate cut-off, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://github.com/ParkerLab/ataqv
  column: duplicate_fraction
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average duplicate fraction, with the median and the highest library

- component: card
  title: Median fragment length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the per-library median fragment length, and the box shows the spread. It answers whether the libraries were tagmented to a similar size.
    How to read: libraries should be close together. A library far from the box has a different fragment size profile, so open the fragment ladder.
  column: median_fragment_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median of the library medians, with their spread

- component: table
  title: ATAC quality metrics per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its TSS enrichment, read yield, fractions of mitochondrial and duplicate reads, share of alignments in peaks and peak statistics. It answers the exact numbers an ATAC library is judged on and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by TSS enrichment or by reads in peaks to find the libraries to inspect first.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tss_profile
  title: Coverage around transcription start sites
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: its aggregate read coverage in a window centred on every transcription start site, scaled so the flanks of the window average 1. It answers whether the reads concentrate at start sites.
    How to read: a good library has a sharp spike at the TSS standing well above the flanks. A low or broad shoulder means weak or diffuse enrichment, so check the fragment ladder and the share of reads in peaks.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker is the TSS at position 0. The height of the curve at it is the TSS enrichment score, as ataqv scales the profile by the mean of the 100 bp at each end of the window.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ParkerLab/ataqv/master/src/cpp/Metrics.cpp
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: TSS
    x_title: Distance from the TSS (bp)
    y_title: Normalised coverage
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: position
    y: coverage

- component: figure
  title: Coverage around transcription start sites
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the aggregate read coverage around start sites. It answers the same question as the profile as a plain curve.
    How to read: look for a spike at zero over a flat baseline of about one. A broad bump without a spike means diffuse signal.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: position
    y: coverage
    color: sample
    labels:
      position: Distance from the TSS (bp)
      coverage: Normalised coverage
      sample: Library

- component: card
  title: Enrichment at the TSS
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average normalised coverage exactly at the start site, which is the TSS enrichment score. It answers how strong the signal is at the centre of the profile.
    How to read: higher is better. A library below the lower line has weak enrichment.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-offs are the ENCODE values for the GRCh38 RefSeq TSS annotation, 7 and above is ideal, 5 to 7 acceptable and under 5 concerning. Other annotations use other values.
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/atac-seq/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ParkerLab/ataqv/master/src/cpp/Metrics.cpp
  column: coverage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 7.0
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 5.0
  filter_expr: col('position') == 0
  caption: average coverage at the TSS, with the lowest and highest library

- component: card
  title: Spread of TSS enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median coverage at the start site over libraries, and the box shows how they spread. It answers whether the libraries enrich alike.
    How to read: a library far below the box has weaker signal than its peers. Open the profile to see whether it lacks a spike or has a high background.
  column: coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('position') == 0
  caption: median enrichment at the TSS, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Highest point of the profile
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest coverage anywhere in the window, and the bars rank the libraries reaching the highest point. It answers which libraries have the sharpest peak.
    How to read: the highest point is normally at or next to the TSS. If a library peaks elsewhere, the profile is noisy and its enrichment score is not reliable.
  column: coverage
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: highest coverage in the window, with the libraries ranked

- component: table
  title: Coverage profile values
  description: |-
    Each row is a position in the window around start sites with the normalised coverage of a library. It answers the exact values behind the profile.
    How to read: filter to position 0 to read the enrichment of every library.
